dek: DevDay 2026 brought new agents, a $500 tier, and no IPO promise.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: OpenAI held its DevDay 2026 keynote in *San Francisco* on September 29th, led by CEO Sam Altman.

slides.label: Meet Dots
slides.text: OpenAI launched *Dots*, an always-on AI agent that works across *4,000+ apps*, rivaling Meta's Muse.

slides.label: Paid Access Only
slides.text: Unlike free-to-use Muse, Dots starts *paid-only* for ChatGPT Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise users.

slides.label: Bigger Plans
slides.text: OpenAI's CFO says the goal is to bring Dots to its *entire consumer base* down the line.

slides.label: New Numbers
slides.text: OpenAI added a *$500/month* Pro tier with Ultrafast speed, as ChatGPT hit *1.2 billion* weekly users.

slides.label: No IPO Yet
slides.text: Altman says OpenAI *won't go public* until it can make confident safety claims, with no timeline set.

slides.label: Tense Backdrop
slides.text: The launch follows reports of AI agents *hacking outside companies* and protesters outside DevDay chanting 'people over profit.'

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: As AI tools get *pricier and gatekept*, access gaps widen for underrepresented builders trying to compete.

question: Would you pay $500 a month for an AI agent that never IPOs?
caption_instagram:
OpenAI just dropped a new AI agent, and it's not free for everyone.

At its DevDay 2026 keynote in San Francisco, CEO Sam Altman unveiled Dots, an always-on assistant that works across more than 4,000 apps to rival Meta's Muse. Unlike Muse, Dots is starting out paid-only, limited to ChatGPT Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise subscribers, with OpenAI's CFO saying wider consumer access is coming later.

The company also rolled out a $500 a month Pro tier, revealed ChatGPT now has 1.2 billion weekly users, and confirmed there's no IPO on the horizon until it can make stronger safety promises. All of this comes as reports surface of AI agents hacking outside companies, and protesters gathered outside DevDay demanding OpenAI put people over profit.

For underrepresented builders already priced out of top-tier AI tools, access gaps like this hit different.

Would you pay $500 a month for an AI agent that never IPOs?

OpenAI's DevDay 2026 keynote in San Francisco dropped a lot of signal for founders and operators watching the AI agent race.

The headline launch is Dots, an always-on AI agent built on OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model, working across more than 4,000 apps to compete with Meta's Muse. The catch: Dots is launching paid-only, reserved for ChatGPT Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise subscribers, with OpenAI's CFO confirming broader consumer access is a future goal, not a current reality.

OpenAI also introduced a $500 a month Pro tier, reported 1.2 billion weekly ChatGPT users, and CEO Sam Altman reaffirmed there's no IPO timeline until the company can make confident safety claims, a stance shaped by recent reports of AI agents hacking outside companies.

For founders building on top of these platforms, pricing tiers like this decide who gets early access to the tools shaping the next product cycle.
